key_insight: This paper shows that inverse problems in chaotic systems can be tackled by learning a bidirectional stochastic mapping between initial and final states, rather than trying to force a single deterministic inverse. Bi-CFM helps recover plausible initial conditions even when the dynamics are unstable and non-unique.
problem_solved: It addresses the long-standing challenge of inferring initial conditions from observed final states in chaotic dynamical systems, where the inverse is ill-posed, highly sensitive, and often non-unique.
method: Uses Bidirectional Conditional Flow Matching (Bi-CFM) to learn mappings in both forward and reverse directions between distributions of states.
Models the stochasticity of chaotic evolution so the inverse process can represent multiple valid solutions instead of one fixed answer.
Trains a conditional generative flow to capture the relationship between initial and final states under chaotic dynamics.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a practical framework for solving inverse problems in systems where classical methods fail due to chaos and ambiguity. It can improve state estimation, forecasting, and scientific discovery in physics-driven and dynamical system applications.

paper_title: Solving Inverse Problems of Chaotic Systems with Bidirectional Conditional Flow Matching
paper_authors: Peiyan Hu, Jian Zhang, Jiashu Pan, Ruiqi Feng, Tao Zhang
